response.title: which power station runs a portable ice maker the longest
response.answer:
To run a portable ice maker for the longest time, you want a high-capacity LiFePO₄ power station with an AC outlet.

The most important specification is battery capacity (Wh), not maximum output wattage (W).

Most countertop portable ice makers consume approximately 100–200 watts while actively making ice, although actual consumption varies by model and compressor cycle.

For comparison, I'll use a 150W ice maker and assume 85% usable battery energy after inverter losses.

Power station capacity

These are continuous-operation estimates. An ice maker that cycles its compressor off periodically could last longer.

Which would I choose?

For maximum runtime without adding batteries, the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X wins among these options. But for an ordinary portable ice maker, it is probably excessive in size and cost.

For camping or outdoor use, a smaller 2,000–3,000Wh unit may be a better balance.

Two questions to narrow this down:

What brand/model of portable ice maker do you have (GE Opal, Frigidaire, Euhomy, etc.)?

How long do you need it to run—8 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, or as long as possible?

With those details, I can compare the actual runtime and cost of suitable power stations.
